children: Pacific Gas and Electric Company and Southern California Edison said they may cut power for hundreds of thousands of customers due to a heightened risk of wildfires.
The disclosures came after the National Weather Service issued a red-flag warning--denoting that conditions are ideal for wildfire combustion and rapid spread--for parts of Southern California.
PG&E on Wednesday said it may cut power for about 88,000 customers in portions of 29 countries across the state.

Meanwhile, Southern California Edison said it will consider power shutoffs for about 245,000 customers, or about 5% of its total customers, across Los Angeles, Ventura, Kern, Tulare and Santa Barbara counties.

Both utilities said they plan to continue updating the scope of their respective shutoffs as weather conditions evolve. Currently, the companies are monitoring a potential dry offshore wind event, forecast to extend from Wednesday evening to Saturday afternoon.
